bugs: An unauthenticated GET /api/webhook-events without Accept: application/json returns 500 because route [login] is not defined; no redirectGuestsTo/API guard is configured (routes/web.php:18-19). Confirmed with a probe.
The receipt hardcodes the currency as 'EUR' whatever the order or provider currency is (app/Notifications/PaymentReceipt.php:25).
retryUntil is fixed at 1 hour from dispatch (ProcessWebhookEvent.php:43-46), so with a queue backlog over an hour, or long rate-limit throttling, jobs fail without ever calling the provider.

If no Order matches, firstOrFail throws ModelNotFoundException, so the job retries up to 5 times and then stores the vague error 'No query results for model [App\Models\Order].' (ProcessWebhookEvent.php:97).
antipatterns: Writes a custom webhooks:prune command with a processedBefore scope instead of using Prunable/MassPrunable with model:prune (app/Console/Commands/PruneWebhookEvents.php:10-21).

Adds an extra RecoverStuckWebhookEvents command and an every-10-minutes schedule the task did not ask for (app/Console/Commands/RecoverStuckWebhookEvents.php, routes/console.php:12), which is over-engineering.
Event types are bare string literals in in_array and match instead of a backed enum (app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:70,99-103).
Hand-rolled transitionTo() does query-builder updates that bypass Eloquent model events and then calls refresh() (app/Models/Order.php:67-77), adding ceremony.

Tests mock Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\Job with Mockery instead of using withFakeQueueInteractions()/assertFailed()/assertReleased() (tests/Feature/ProcessWebhookEventTest.php:157-159,176-178,192-194).
The README section is appended after the untouched Laravel boilerplate (README.md).
The admin API route lives in web.php behind session auth instead of routes/api.php (routes/web.php:18).
strengths: Status-guarded conditional order transitions plus lockForUpdate inside a transaction: a late payment.failed cannot overwrite a paid order, and the receipt is sent only on a real transition.
Receipt is a ShouldQueueAfterCommit notification, so it is never sent for a rolled-back transaction.
Handles 429 by releasing with the provider's Retry-After; 4xx fails permanently and 5xx is rethrown for the backoff [5,30,120,600] with MaxExceptions(5).
Uses the WithoutOverlapping and RateLimited middleware, WithoutRelations, DeleteWhenMissingModels, and #[Scope] attributes.
Scheduled tasks use onOneServer and withoutOverlapping, and the README covers timeout nesting and retry_after well.
42 tests, the largest suite, covering replays, late events, 429, 4xx, 5xx recovery and stuck recovery.

bugs: The 'processing' status is never saved: forceFill(['status' => Processing])->increment('attempts') only persists the incremented column, so after a 5xx the event stays 'pending' (ProcessWebhookEvent.php:51). Confirmed with a probe.

The PaymentReceipt notification is not queued and not after-commit (app/Notifications/PaymentReceipt.php:10), and the order update plus notify are not in a transaction, so the mail is sent inline inside the worker job.
If no order matches, the job fails permanently on the first attempt (ProcessWebhookEvent.php:81-84), so a webhook that arrives before its order row exists is lost without a retry.
An event with an empty data object ({}) is rejected with 422 by the 'required' array rule (PaymentWebhookRequest.php:14), which can cause endless provider redeliveries.

Tries(50) also counts RateLimited and WithoutOverlapping releases, and WithoutOverlapping uses the default releaseAfter(0), so under sustained throttling the job can run out of tries without hitting a real error.
antipatterns: Uses forceFill(...)->increment() and assumes the filled attributes are saved too (app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:51).
The admin API route lives in web.php behind session auth instead of routes/api.php (routes/web.php:16-18).
Unknown event types are silently marked processed with no record (ProcessWebhookEvent.php:53-55).
postWebhook test helper hand-builds HTTP_ server variables with collect()->mapWithKeys (tests/Pest.php:57-73) where withHeaders()->call() would do.
Tests the backoff by reflecting on attributes, which only asserts configuration (tests/Feature/ProcessWebhookEventTest.php:117-123).
strengths: The simplest implementation: createOrFirst on a unique event_id with dispatch only when wasRecentlyCreated, and a thin controller.
Uses MassPrunable with Schedule::command('model:prune') daily, plus queue:prune-failed.

Job configured with modern queue attributes (#[Tries, MaxExceptions, Backoff, Timeout, DeleteWhenMissingModels]) and the WithoutOverlapping and RateLimited middleware with a shared perSecond(10) limiter.
Refunds are idempotent through a unique webhook_event_id with firstOrCreate inside a transaction; 4xx fails permanently and 5xx/429 retry.
The only implementation that configures redirectGuestsTo, so unauthenticated API access returns 401 instead of 500.
Clean dedicated README with a Supervisor config, retry_after/timeout guidance, queue:restart and the scheduler.
Pest tests use a global beforeEach with Http::preventStrayRequests, datasets, and lock/rate-limit behaviour tests.

bugs: An unauthenticated GET /api/webhook-events without Accept: application/json returns 500 because route [login] is not defined (routes/web.php:16-18, bootstrap/app.php). Confirmed with a probe.

OrderFactory has no user_id, so Order::factory()->create() throws a NOT NULL violation and every caller must chain ->for($user) (database/factories/OrderFactory.php:14-22); RefundFactory likewise has no order or webhook_event.

PaymentProviderClient::payment() declares an array return type, so a 200 response with an empty body throws TypeError (app/Services/PaymentProviderClient.php:17-25). It is then retried as a generic exception.
retryUntil is fixed at 2 hours from dispatch, so a backlog longer than that fails jobs without processing them (ProcessWebhookEvent.php:47-50).
If no order matches, the job fails permanently with no retry (ProcessWebhookEvent.php:71-75), so an out-of-order delivery is lost.
antipatterns: The migration is named create_orders_table but also creates webhook_events and refunds (database/migrations/2026_11_07_000002_create_orders_table.php).
The README section is inserted into the untouched Laravel boilerplate (README.md).
Global const declarations in Pest test files (PAYMENT_URL, SECRET) can collide across files (tests/Feature/ProcessWebhookEventTest.php:21, tests/Feature/ReceiveWebhookTest.php:8).
The admin API route lives in web.php with session auth (routes/web.php:16).
The StoreWebhookEvent action class is a small extra layer for what amounts to createOrFirst plus dispatch (app/Actions/StoreWebhookEvent.php).
strengths: Receipt is a ShouldQueueAfterCommit notification with its own Tries/Backoff attributes, sent from inside a DB::transaction, and skipped when the order is already paid, so the receipt is never sent twice.
Job uses retryUntil together with MaxExceptions(5) and Backoff([5,30,120,600]), so middleware releases do not burn the retry budget; this is documented clearly.
WithoutOverlapping keyed by event_id with releaseAfter(15)/expireAfter(120), plus the RateLimited middleware and a shared Limit::perSecond(10).
Deletes the stored event if dispatch throws, so the provider's redelivery is not swallowed as a duplicate.
Uses MassPrunable with a daily model:prune, isFinal() on the status enum, a scopeWithStatus scope, and typed status()/perPage() accessors on the FormRequest.
Tests use withFakeQueueInteractions()->assertFailed(), datasets, Http::sequence, and include an end-to-end sync-queue test (38 tests).

v.rationale: All three pass their own suites (impl-2: 34 tests, impl-3: 38, impl-1: 42). All three share the same core: createOrFirst on a unique event_id, a job using the WithoutOverlapping and RateLimited middleware with a perSecond(10) limiter, failed() writing the error to the event, and a policy-gated index with a FormRequest. impl-3 ranks first: it covers the focus area most completely (an after-commit queued receipt sent inside a transaction and never twice, retryUntil plus MaxExceptions so releases don't burn tries, cleanup if dispatch fails, model:prune). Its bugs are peripheral: a 500 for unauthenticated non-JSON requests, a broken OrderFactory default, and a boilerplate README. impl-2 is the simplest and cleanest, and the only one returning 401 instead of 500 for guests. But its 'processing' status is never saved (forceFill + increment), its receipt is neither queued nor after-commit, and Tries(50) can be used up by throttle releases. impl-1 is the most defensive (status-guarded transitions, lockForUpdate, 429 Retry-After). It falls short on idioms: a hand-written prune command instead of Prunable, an extra stuck-event recovery command, string-literal event types, Mockery job mocks, and a hardcoded EUR currency. It also shares the 500-on-guest bug.
